speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury you described—getting caught and pulled forcefully—sounds like it could have caused a dislocation or a fracture. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and can you move your finger normally now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Lag at DIP Joint).

The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint combined with the history of a direct avulsive pull and the finger resting in extension is classic for an extensor tendon avulsion. I will not request further imaging as the clinical presentation is pathognomonic, but please ensure the finger remains immobilized in extension.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
